newsitem.title: UK: Mexican Brady debt unchanged ahead of elections.
newsitem.headline: Mexican Brady debt unchanged ahead of elections.

text.p: Mexican Brady bonds were unchanged in thin trade on Friday before the country's mid-term congressional elections on Sunday but analysts said they did not expect any fallout even if there is a shift in power.

"It has been clear cut from the polls that the market always will react in advance rather than (on) confirmation so I would be surprised if there was any great shakeout," said Neil Lockwood, emerging market analyst at ANZ Investment Bank in London.

On Sunday, Mexicans will vote for a new lower house of Congress, a quarter of the Senate, six state governors and, for the first time a mayor of Mexico City which had been previously filled by a presidential nominee.

The Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) could lose its lower house majority for the first time since 1929 but experts said they did not believe it would have any impact on Mexican economic policy.
"I think the balance of power is going to shift but I think most people don't think it will have a huge impact on economic policy," said Lockwood.
Mexican pars, which were one of the best performers on Thursday closing up 1-1/8 in New York at 79-5/8 bid, were unchanged.

Market experts attributed those gains to a spectacular rally in the U.S. Treasury market after a weak U.S. unemployment report slimmed the odds of a credit tightening at the next Federal Open Market Committee meeting in August.

"At the moment, people are stronger believers in the upside. A lot of crossover buyers are continuing to look at Mexico as perhaps one of the first Latins to join the emerged world and so I think that sentiment is outweighing any real concerns" of the outcome of the elections, said a trader at a European bank.
Although activity remained extremely thin because of the U.S. Independence Day holiday on Friday, traders said bullish sentiment should continue next week.
"We should come back and retrace some holes next week but we expect quite a solid Treasury market which will put a strong bid into the Bradies," the trader said.
